issues.t: Timing chain rattle
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine that sounds a bit like a diesel, most noticeable for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes with a check engine light for camshaft timing.
issues.why: The timing chain, its tensioner and guides wear on all of MINI's 1.6L engines of this era, especially when oil changes are stretched out. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: Do not ignore a rattle that lasts or gets louder. Have a shop inspect the chain and tensioner soon, because a chain that jumps or breaks can bend valves and ruin the engine. Change synthetic oil every 5,000-7,500 miles.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the car, a sweet smell, the coolant level warning, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The engine water pump is one of the most common failures on these MINIs, and owners report leaks from as early as 20,000 miles. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and do not drive if the temperature warning comes on. Many shops replace the thermostat at the same time since the labor overlaps.

issues.t: Thermostat or thermostat housing failure
issues.sym: Check engine light with a thermostat code, the engine running hot or slow to warm up, cooling fans running constantly or after shutdown, or coolant leaking near the housing.
issues.why: The electronically controlled thermostat and its plastic housing fail on these 1.6L engines, and some cars also crack nearby coolant hoses. Owners report failures from about 23,000 miles. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: If the engine overheats, pull over and turn it off. Otherwise have the codes read and replace the thermostat soon. Confirm the right part by VIN, since several versions exist.

issues.t: Cracked oil filter housing leaking oil and coolant
issues.sym: Oil and coolant leaking around the top-front of the engine, oil in the coolant, a burning smell, or a low oil or coolant warning.
issues.why: The oil filter housing, which also contains the engine oil cooler, can crack or its gaskets can fail, letting oil and coolant leak and soak the wiring harness below. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: Check both oil and coolant levels. Do not keep driving if either is dropping quickly. Fix it early, before leaking oil damages the wiring harness and drives the bill up.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Loss of power, hesitation or stalling, a long crank before it starts, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The turbo engine's high-pressure fuel pump, which feeds the direct injectors, fails on these MINIs. Several Countryman owners report it between about 38,000 and 92,000 miles. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: If the car loses power in traffic, get to a safe place. Have the fuel pressure checked; ask for the latest software and the correct updated pump for your VIN.

issues.t: Turbo oil feed line leak
issues.sym: Oil smell or smoke from under the hood, oil residue around the turbocharger, and later a whining turbo or loss of boost.
issues.why: The factory oil line that feeds the turbocharger leaks at its banjo-bolt fittings with age. A leak can starve the turbo of oil, and long oil change intervals make turbo failure more likely. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: Have any oil leak near the turbo fixed promptly. Many owners replace the stock line with an improved braided line. Keep oil changes at 7,500 miles or less.

issues.t: Oil leak from VANOS or oil pump solenoid
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine, oil on the front of the engine, or a burning-oil smell. A failing VANOS solenoid can also cause a check engine light and rough idle.
issues.why: The solenoids that control the variable valve timing (VANOS) and the oil pump leak oil at their seals, and owners often mistake the leak for something else. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: Have the source pinpointed before replacing parts. Most fixes are a solenoid or seal. Keep the oil topped up in the meantime.

issues.t: Misfires from failing ignition coils
issues.sym: Shaking or stumbling, especially when accelerating, rough idle, and a check engine light, which may flash.
issues.why: Ignition coils fail on these engines, often one at a time, and worn spark plugs speed it up. Countryman owners report coil failures from about 60,000 miles. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Replace the failed coil, and the spark plugs if they are due.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket or crankcase vent leak
issues.sym: Oil seeping around the top of the engine, a burning-oil smell, rough idle, or a check engine light for a vacuum leak.
issues.why: The plastic valve cover, its gasket and the crankcase vent hoses crack and harden with heat over time. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: Fix it before oil drips onto the hot exhaust. A cracked valve cover usually means replacing the cover with its built-in vent parts.

issues.t: Cranks but will not start (eccentric shaft wear)
issues.sym: The non-turbo engine cranks normally but will not start, or starts and runs badly, with a check engine light.
issues.why: The non-turbo 1.6L uses Valvetronic variable valve lift. Wear in its eccentric shaft or sensor can keep the valves from opening far enough to start. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: Have the codes read by a shop familiar with MINI. Unplugging the eccentric shaft sensor is only a get-home trick, not a repair.

issues.t: Front differential failure (ALL4)
issues.sym: Grinding, whining or clunking from the front of the car, especially when pulling away, and in the worst case loss of drive.
issues.why: The front differential on all-wheel-drive models can fail, with owners reporting it around 100,000 miles. The Paceman is the two-door version of the 2011-2016 Countryman and shares its engines and running gear, so Countryman owner reports apply.
issues.next: Have the noise checked soon and do not wait for it to seize. Changing the differential and transfer case fluid more often than the factory suggests may help.

issues.t: Footwell module failure: lights, windows and signals stop working
issues.sym: Turn signals, headlights, high beams or power windows stop working, a false "door open" warning, or the battery keeps going flat.
issues.why: The footwell module (FRM) that runs the lights and windows can fail, often because moisture corrupts it. A Paceman owner was told the extended FRM warranty (10 years or 156,000 miles) had run out and had to pay for the fix.
issues.next: Missing turn signals and headlights are a safety risk, so avoid driving at night until fixed. Ask a MINI dealer whether your car is still inside the extended FRM coverage. Clear the sunroof drains so water does not return.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cabin from clogged sunroof drains
issues.sym: Wet carpet or a damp smell, water dripping inside, and electrical faults such as a no-start or wipers that stop working.
issues.why: When the sunroof drain tubes clog, water overflows into the cabin and can damage the electronic modules under the carpet. A 2015 Paceman owner reported water through the sunroof damaging circuit boards, stopping the wipers and leaving the car unable to start.
issues.next: Clear the drains with compressed air or trimmer line and dry the carpet right away. If the wipers or lights fail, do not drive in rain or at night until repaired. Check which modules got wet.

issues.t: Door handle breaks and door will not open or close
issues.sym: A door will not open from outside, or will not latch shut.
issues.why: A 2015 Paceman owner reported door handles failing twice in about three years. The outside handle cable stretches or the handle mechanism breaks.
issues.next: Do not drive with a door that will not latch. Have the handle and cable replaced; check the other door too.

issues.t: Clutch or dual-mass flywheel wear (manual)
issues.sym: Clutch slipping (revs rise without more speed), shudder when pulling away, or a rattle at idle that goes away when you press the clutch.
issues.why: MINIs of this era wear out clutches and dual-mass flywheels fairly quickly, especially in city driving.
issues.next: If the clutch slips, avoid hard acceleration and get a quote. The flywheel is usually replaced with the clutch.

issues.t: Rear tires wear on the inside edges
issues.sym: The rear tires wear unevenly on the inner edges, and the car may feel less planted.
issues.why: The rear lower control arm bushings stretch, tilting the top of the rear wheels inward (negative camber).
issues.next: Check the tires often. An alignment check will confirm it; adjustable arms or new bushings fix it.

issues.t: Front strut mount worn: clunk and one side sits low
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps from the front, and one front corner sitting lower than the other.
issues.why: The front upper strut mounts stretch and tear with age.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replace the mounts in pairs and get an alignment.

issues.t: Rear hatch will not open or pops open
issues.sym: The hatch does not open when you press the button, or it opens on its own.
issues.why: The rubber boot over the hatch switch dries out and cracks, letting water into the switch.
issues.next: Replace the hatch switch. Until then, check the hatch is shut before driving.

issues.t: Hood scoop warps from turbo heat
issues.sym: The hood scoop on the Cooper S or JCW warps or sags.
issues.why: Heat from the turbocharger below the scoop distorts the plastic over time.
issues.next: This is cosmetic. Replace the scoop if it bothers you.

issues.t: Cowl trim near the wipers cracks
issues.sym: The plastic panel at the base of the windshield cracks or warps.
issues.why: The cowl trim overheats and cracks with age.
issues.next: Cosmetic, but a broken cowl lets leaves and water reach the area below. Replace left and right pieces together.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning light stays on
issues.sym: The tire pressure warning stays on or comes back even after the tires are set correctly.
issues.why: UK inspection data shows Paceman tire pressure monitoring faults at more than twice the average rate, often from a failed sensor or one that was not reset.
issues.next: Check all tire pressures with a gauge first. If they are right, reset the system as shown in the owner's manual; if it returns, have the sensors checked.

issues.t: Headlight washers stop working
issues.sym: The headlight washer jets do not spray when you wash the windshield with the lights on.
issues.why: UK inspection data shows Paceman headlamp washer failures at several times the average rate, usually from a failed pump, leaking line or stuck jet.
issues.next: Check the washer fluid level first. A shop can test the pump and lines.

issues.t: Brake pads wear quickly
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding from the brakes, or the brake wear warning coming on earlier than expected.
issues.why: UK inspection data shows Paceman brake pad failures at more than twice the average rate.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors checked when the wear light comes on and replace the wear sensor with the pads.
